top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye is one bounded invention, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, with a measured outcome near 1e-18 reproduced independently by several national laboratories and already used for tests of constants, relativity and relativistic geodesy. Katori for the concept and first realisation and Ye for taking strontium lattice clocks to record accuracy and stability gives a clean two-name allocation, and a citation naming the lattice and the magic wavelength separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The overlap with those prizes is a real reservation, but it is a drafting matter and does not outweigh a mature, well-attributed achievement, so no award ranks below it.
